name: manual_1d5838
claim: Do not fire a manual git push immediately after a backgrounded shell command that itself ends in git push — check whether the background task actually completed first (via its notification/output), or the manual push races the async one and 'remote rejected: cannot lock ref, is at X but expected Y' looks like a real branch-divergence conflict when it is only local ref-tracking staleness from your own in-flight push.

decisions.notes: Hit this exact race on PT PR #241's locale-fix push: the backgrounded 'commit && push' had already landed f872d2ef on origin by the time a manual follow-up 'git push' ran against a stale local view of origin, producing a scary-looking rejection that a fetch immediately resolved as a non-issue.
